title: Seatquaa: Creek-Mouth Wetland Place Name
summary: Seatquaa is a place-name connected with land at the mouth of a creek or tidal stream. The name helps explain how Native geographic language described estuaries, creek mouths, marshes, and movement through the south shore.
address_label: South shore creek-mouth landscape, Freeport-Merrick-Bellmore area
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as a south shore wetland/place-name learning point.
why_this_matters: Seatquaa presents the south shore as Native geography: creek mouths, marshes, and bay edges were named and meaningful places for fishing, shellfishing, travel, and settlement. The word opens a way to understand wetlands as cultural landscapes.
introduction_content: Seatquaa belongs to the Freeport-Merrick-Bellmore creek-mouth landscape and helps explain wetland geography and Native place description. The name should not be reduced to one modern block or shoreline.
translation_content:
Why Place Names Matter

“It is common knowledge that the act of naming places is in fact a way to control and infuse space, with particular belief-systems and values.”

— Elisabetta Dall’Ò, Historicizing vulnerability: place-names, risk and memory in the Mont Blanc area (2019), Article introduction
